headline: In a backtest the foundation models may have seen in training, Chronos-2's day-ahead demand forecast had 1.31 times the daily error of NESO's (90% interval 1.26 to 1.36), and a supplier that bought it instead of NESO's would have **neither clearly gained nor lost** (9 £ per GWh of demand, 90% interval −11 to 28); for the weather regression the figure was −1 £ per GWh (−20 to 18). Where Chronos-2 disagreed with NESO most (the largest quarter of its disagreements), each MWh of disagreement was worth 0.07 £ (−0.80 to 0.90), against −0.45 £ (−0.91 to 0.07) in the smallest quarter.
